notes: Targets NOT placed (no facility row, no opened page with city and state): (a) Hitachi Energy Pinetops, NC: one search returned no result for Pinetops. (b) Hitachi Energy Pennsylvania: no result. (c) GE Vernova/Prolec GE Pennsylvania, Pittsfield MA, Hickory NC: no result from one search; Prolec GE Goldsboro NC is already in the first pass. (d) LS Electric Chesapeake VA: the only result was a Korean-language report of an LS Greenlink groundbreaking on 2025-04-28 by LS Cable and System, not LS Electric; not placed. (e) Howard Industries Laurel MS: the 2025 release is datelined Laurel and lists Laurel as the mailing address, but describes no Laurel facility. (f) ERMCO 2019 Dyersburg expansion ($12M, 150 jobs) and the October 2024 three-phase project (400 jobs) appeared only in search snippets, not on an opened page. (g) Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works ($170M electrical project, Lyndora PA) appeared only in a search snippet; not placed.

Schneider Electric (plantservices article, 2025-04-01, opened): US locations and product lines are stated only as paraphrase, not verbatim, so no facility rows were written. Page says: Welcome, NC modernized facility to produce switchgear and power distribution gear; El Paso, TX expanded capacity for switchgear and power distribution gear; Mt. Juliet, TN new medium-voltage facility; Columbia, MO added plant space for circuit breakers; Fairfield, OH advanced manufacturing; Raleigh, NC robotics center; Houston, TX innovation center; Andover, MA labs. Page does not mention transformers. Total: planned investment of over $700 million in U.S. operations through 2027, over 1,000 jobs (quoted verbatim). Use this for the switchgear target if a verbatim plant-level quote is needed.

Eaton Bellevue, NE switchgear plant: manufacturing.net and renewableenergyworld.com both returned HTTP 403 on fetch. Search-snippet facts (not verified on an opened page): 370,000 sq ft, more than $30 million, over 200 jobs, production in H1 2027. Not written as a row. Eaton Henrico County, VA (more than $50 million, static transfer switches and PDUs, production 2027) is also snippet-only and is not a transformer or switchgear plant.

Hitachi Alamo, TN: the tn.gov page opened names Crockett County and does not name Alamo; the city in this row comes from the Hitachi release title in search results and is NOT verified on an opened page. Investment conflict: the tn.gov release says an initial $97 million (used here); a Hitachi release in search results says $106 million. The bushings are transformer components, not complete transformers.

Hitachi Bland, VA: the Area Development summary gives $22.5 million and 120 jobs, and states that the project increases transformer production at the existing Bland site and adds a warehouse in Atkins. It does not name the product line.

Siemens Energy Charlotte: the city of Charlotte release page returned an Akamai bot-protection block and could not be opened. Search snippets report a later February 2026 expansion ($421 million across North Carolina, about 500 jobs) and a 2024 job figure of 475 in Canary Media. Neither was opened, so neither is used. The row uses the 2024 Manufacturing Dive figures only (investment $149.8 million, 559 jobs). Production start dates conflict across sources (early 2026 vs. early 2027).

Prolec GE Shreveport: the 2023 announcement quote is used. Snippets report a completed $34 million expansion in November 2024, with the facility described as 500,000 sq ft and more than 270 new jobs. These were NOT verified on an opened page. Status is set to expansion for that reason and should be re-checked.

Howard Industries: the Howard release says over $230 million (the governor cites $236 million) and at least 450 full-time jobs across Clarke, Jones and Simpson counties. Those are regional totals, so per-plant investment and jobs are null. The Quitman and Ellisville rows carry the same quote. The release does not say what either facility makes; the 'amorphous' Quitman name is taken from the facility name only. A $100 million Quitman figure and the 400,000 sq ft addition appeared in search snippets only, not on the opened page.

LS Electric: the Bastrop page opened describes a 58,925 sq ft technical center to support U.S. operations, not a factory, so the row's product is null and its status is operating. Snippets report a further $240 million by 2030 for Bastrop production (Korea Times) and $168 million (March 2026) to triple switchgear capacity at the Utah plant. Neither was opened, so neither is written.

Cleveland-Cliffs Zanesville: the status 'operating' rests on the April 2024 release's present-tense description of Butler and Zanesville as plants that make GOES. The 'possibility of future investments' sentence is not an announced expansion, and the row records no investment. Operating status was not re-checked for 2025 or 2026.

Hammond Power Solutions Fort Worth: the lease was signed and the company expects production in stages from Q4 2027, with full operation in Q1 2028. Jobs are not stated. Projected capacity is $283-284 million a year (T&D World). The Monterrey, Mexico expansion is outside the US scope and not written.

SPX Transformer Solutions Waukesha: the expansion is from 2012. No 2025 Waukesha expansion turned up in one search. The page gives about 432,000 sq ft of added floor space and a 500-ton crane capacity, and says output rose by about half. Floor space and crane are not written as requirement rows because the page's date (2012) makes them dated facts.

JST Power Equipment Wytheville: the Business Wire release returned 403 on fetch. Transformer-technology.com (published 2026-05-27) gives the Fairview Industrial Park location, about 45,000 sq ft across two buildings, the 11th US location, a ribbon-cutting on 2026-05-19, and an initial 35-50 workers (not written as a number, because it is a range). No investment figure. The product is not stated on the opened page; the search snippet's 'three-phase padmount' is unverified.

Virginia Transformer Muscle Shoals, AL is NOT one of the named targets. It is an added find from the Alabama governor's release (opened): 600,000 sq ft plant, about 90 acres, 1,100 jobs, production expected January 2028, a dedicated Norfolk Southern rail spur, and about $4.5 million for park site work under the Growing Alabama tax credit. The release does not state the plant's own investment. Not in the first-pass list, so it is included.
No DOE, LPO or other federal award was found for any row in this set.
Query budget: about 34 tool calls used (ToolSearch and Read excluded from the count).
